records.title: Birmingham: sustaining a group of co-producers
records.status: Published practitioner account with named client testimony
records.situation: Birmingham commissioned a co-produced review of day opportunities following the pandemic.
records.intervention: RedQuadrant recruited and supported people with lived experience and carers to co-lead the review. The published account describes a second phase and a 23-member Empowering People Team.
records.result: The account reports that findings informed commissioning and improvement plans, and that members continued into other co-production work. The client describes growing confidence and further involvement.
records.limit: These are practitioner and client accounts, rather than an independent impact evaluation. The published evidence does not isolate effects on all day-opportunity users.
records.artefact: Public case account, pp. 1–4: engagement, reports, and subsequent work
records.followup: What decisions changed, whose views were missed, and what resources now sustain the group?

records.title: Gateshead: reviewing commissioning across directorates
records.status: Published practitioner account with client testimony
records.situation: Adult and children’s social care commissioned a review of commissioning practice.
records.intervention: RedQuadrant used a workshop-based assessment drawing on PSTA’s commissioning approach and developed recommendations with council officers.
records.result: The published case reports acceptance of recommendations and development of a commissioning strategy, with a subsequent invitation to review progress.
records.limit: Acceptance and a return commission establish decisions and continued engagement. They do not by themselves establish improved resident outcomes or sustained financial benefits.
records.followup: Which recommendations were implemented, what changed in commissioning decisions, and what evidence do residents and providers offer?

records.title: Hillingdon: Resource Optimisation within wider transformation
records.situation: The organisation needed a consistent way to examine work and choices across services.
records.intervention: Resource Optimisation formed part of a wider RedQuadrant transformation operating system used across more than 40 services.
records.result: The existing public account establishes reported organisation-wide use of an integrated approach.
records.limit: The public account does not establish that Resource Optimisation alone caused all reported programme results. A method’s contribution needs to be distinguished from the wider programme.
records.artefact: Published method account and Seven Ts decision framework
records.followup: Which work packages changed, what happened to displaced work, and which benefits remained after implementation?

records.title: Bristol: separating identified savings from realised benefits
records.status: RedQuadrant practitioner account; benefits require follow-through
records.situation: Bristol used applied learning, leadership development, and coaching in transformation work.
records.intervention: RedQuadrant’s public service account describes the Applied Programme, Bristol Leads, and development for senior directors.
records.result: The account says the first four cohorts identified savings of more than £11 million.
records.limit: Identified savings are opportunities. This record does not relabel them as implemented or sustained savings, and the public source does not establish a net financial return attributable to training.
records.artefact: Published service account; Bristol learning-set cards in the design portfolio
records.followup: For each proposal, what was agreed, implemented, and sustained, and what happened to service quality and costs elsewhere?

records.title: SAVVI: useful outputs do not establish adoption at scale
records.status: Public programme record plus independent evaluation
records.situation: SAVVI addresses the cross-agency use of data to identify and support people at risk of poor outcomes.
records.intervention: The Local Digital project record identifies RedQuadrant coaching alongside the council-led programme and describes a playbook, standards, and case work.
records.result: The independent evaluation places SAVVI among projects still being developed and tested during its evaluation period, rather than projects that had achieved cross-sector adoption at scale.
records.limit: This qualifies any inference from producing a reusable standard to achieving widespread use. It is a programme-level finding for the period studied, not an evaluation of an individual coach or a finding about every later deployment.
records.artefact: Local Digital evaluation, section 1.12.6, and the public SAVVI project record
records.followup: Which organisations now use the standard in live work, under what ownership and maintenance arrangements, and with what consequences?

records.title: Westminster: changing access and examining whole cost
records.status: RedQuadrant practitioner account; contemporary follow-up not established
records.situation: Westminster changed its mix of face-to-face and digital access.
records.intervention: RedQuadrant’s public account describes support for closing one-stop shops while developing online and assisted self-service.
records.result: That account reports annual savings of more than £1.2 million and improved online and assisted access.
records.limit: This is a provider-reported historic result. The current public account does not include a dated baseline, independent benefits calculation, distributional effects, or long-term follow-up.
records.followup: Who found access easier or harder, which costs moved to residents or other teams, and how were the claimed annual benefits calculated?
